doctrine: AI video production is a systematic, repeatable engineering discipline, not a creative lottery. The complete operating system: Seven Laws (Quality Chain, Prompt Precision, Consistency, Iteration, Control Hierarchy, Reference Role, Asset-First) that govern all decisions. Image-First Pipeline (Image Generation via Nano Banana Pro/Midjourney -> Image Upscaling via Magnific -> Video Animation via Kling in Professional mode -> Video Upscaling via Topaz Video AI 4K Rhea model). Three prompt frameworks: Five-Part Cinematic (Subject, Action, Environment, Lighting/Atmosphere, Camera Movement), Four-Layer Video (Camera/Framing, Primary Motion, Secondary Motion, Detail/Mood), Constraint Sandwich (Subject Anchor, Shot+Action, Preserve Constraints). Consistency mechanisms: Elements system (multi-angle reference bundles invoked as @element_name), Style Bible Line (one sentence locked across entire project), Reference Image Role Assignment (@image1 for lighting, @image2 for environment, @image3 for character). Kling version routing: 1.0 for precise start/end frames, 2.1 for consistent character narrative, 2.5 Turbo for green-screen, 2.6 for general production + motion transfer + native audio, 3.0 for multi-shot cinema (up to 6 shots, 15 seconds total) + multi-character lip-sync, O1/Omni One for post-production VFX (element removal/addition, relighting, restyle, scene extension). Tool chain: Kling (animation), Nano Banana Pro or Midjourney (reference images), Magnific (upscaling), Topaz Video AI (finisher), ElevenLabs (voice), Runway Act One (lip-sync), Premiere Pro (assembly). Five application domains: Marketing/Product Videos (Element + environment references = infinite campaign variations from single photoshoot), Fashion Content (character + clothing + location Elements), Social Media Talking-Head (eye-catching with dynamic angles via multi-shot), VFX/Compositing (green-screen pipeline, element removal, relighting in post), Pre-Production/Storyboarding (camera angle grids replace manual boards). Monetization: Productized Service (done-for-you high-ticket: trailers, ads, editing), Subscription/Recurring (brand mascot ads, series, character-as-a-service), Licensable Assets (Element libraries, LoRA models, prompt templates), Education (courses on frameworks/vocabulary/workflow). Four mindset shifts required: Gambling to Engineering (structured prompts reduce randomness), Post-Production to Pre-Production (quality ceiling set before generation, not after), Single-Shot to Pipeline Thinking (optimize complete chain, not individual steps), Manual VFX to AI Compositing (prompt-driven operations replace After Effects/Nuke). Implementation: Week 1-2 Foundation (setup accounts, build custom GPTs, practice Five-Part Cinematic on 10+ images, run 3-5 test shots end-to-end), Week 3-4 Production Capability (build Element libraries minimum 4 angles, write Style Bible Line, run full pipeline on real project), Week 5+ Advanced (multi-shot for social, green-screen pipeline, OmniEdit experiments, product-video templates, LoRA training for series). Metrics to track: usable output rate, credits per finished clip, pipeline throughput (concept to finish), character consistency score. Core insight: highest skill is not generating footage but governing consistency across fragmented tools through asset-first thinking.

workflows: Image-First Pipeline: Image Generation (Nano Banana Pro/Midjourney) -> Image Upscaling (Magnific dual-pass) -> Video Animation (Kling Professional mode 5s 16:9) -> Video Upscaling (Topaz Video AI 4K Rhea ProRes)

Multi-shot production: Master scene image -> Character Elements (multi-angle refs) -> Start frame setup -> Multi-shot enable -> Per-shot prompts with @element_name tags -> Per-shot timing -> Generate -> Iterative refinement

Green-screen compositing: Character on green screen (real or AI-generated Kling 2.5 Turbo) -> Kling O1 transformation (upload green-screen + environment reference -> prompt background change preserving character) -> Optional After Effects split-screen VFX

Lip-sync path: Generate video -> Either (1) Type text select AI voice (fast, variable quality) OR (2) Pre-generate voiceover in ElevenLabs, upload audio file to Kling lip-sync (professional standard, more natural)

Element building: Capture 4+ reference images at different angles (close-up, full body, side profile, 3/4 view) minimum one with emotion range needed -> Upload bundle to Kling Elements -> Auto-describe using chat tool -> Identity test (generate short video with @element_name in novel scene) -> Deploy as @element_name in all subsequent prompts

Product video production: Photograph product multiple angles with logo clarity -> Upload as Element -> Add staging/background refs as Elements -> Write prompt combining all Elements + placement + camera + lighting -> Generate -> Use OmniEdit to restyle backgrounds/lighting per campaign without touching product

Pre-visualization storyboarding: Generate key scene image -> Upload as reference -> Prompt for grid of 9-12 camera angles with labels -> Select preferred angles -> Extract and upscale individual frames -> Use next-shot/previous-shot referencing to build sequence with consistent environment/characters -> Animate each frame -> Assemble in NLE

Camera angle exploration: Upload single scene reference -> Prompt image generator for 9-12 different angles labeled (low angle, 3/4 profile, over-shoulder, top-down, etc.) -> Select best angle -> Extract and upscale that specific frame

LoRA training for series work: Collect 10-20 high-quality 1080p frontal-face video sequences of recurring character -> Feed into custom LoRA trainer (approximately 40 minutes training time) -> Reference character name in prompts -> Achieves consistency approaching traditional casting level

Operationalization Phase 1 Foundation: (Week 1-2) Setup (Kling, Nano Banana Pro/Midjourney, Magnific, Topaz Video AI) -> Build custom GPTs (upload Kling + Nano Banana user guides to ChatGPT) -> Test prompt generation -> Practice Five-Part Cinematic on 10+ images -> Run 3-5 image->upscale->animate->review end-to-end tests

Operationalization Phase 2 Production: (Week 3-4) Build Element libraries (minimum 4 angles per Element, one emotion variation for characters) -> Write Style Bible Line -> Test across 5+ generations -> Run full production on real project: storyboard -> image generation -> upscale -> Elements -> animate -> lip-sync -> video upscale -> edit -> Document and templatize best prompts and settings

Operationalization Phase 3 Advanced: (Week 5+) Multi-shot for social + talking-head hooks -> Timing estimate library per shot -> Green-screen compositing tests with live-action -> OmniEdit VFX experiments (relighting, element removal/addition, style transfer) -> Product-video template development for rapid campaign variation -> LoRA training for recurring protagonists
prompts: Five-Part Cinematic structure: [1. Subject: who/what with physical details] [2. Action: what is happening] [3. Environment: where, material and spatial details] [4. Lighting & Atmosphere: sources, temperature, mood, film feel] [5. Camera Movement: shot type, direction, speed, lens behavior]

Four-Layer Video structure: [1. Camera & Framing: shot type and grammar] [2. Primary Motion: main action of subject] [3. Secondary Motion: environmental motion supporting scene] [4. Detail / Mood: film feel, realism cues, atmosphere]

Constraint Sandwich structure: [1. Subject Anchor: element or reference being worked with (@video1, @character, @product)] [2. Shot + Action: what should happen or change] [3. Preserve Constraints: what must NOT be altered (keep camera motion, keep character identity, keep timing, keep body proportions, keep logo integrity)]

Image compositing with references: Upload pose reference + face/character reference simultaneously, describe desired fusion in prompt to eliminate custom pose prompting and give precise compositional control
Lighting transfer reference: Use one reference image for lighting/color and another for composition, combined in single generation to merge color palette of one image with framing of another

Negative prompt universal base: blurry, distorted, unrealistic hands, warped faces, glitchy movement, pixelated, low-quality, jerky camera, unnatural lighting, extra limbs, deformed anatomy, static noise, color banding, compression artifacts, inconsistent proportions
Negative prompt for close-ups (add): asymmetric eyes, melting features, wandering facial features, crossed eyes
Negative prompt for hand-in-frame shots (add): extra fingers, missing fingers, fused fingers, malformed hands
Negative prompt for action shots (add): motion smearing, trailing ghost limbs, teleporting objects
Negative prompt for multi-character shots (add): character blending, identity swap, face merging
Midjourney style reference at low weight: Use --sref [image] --sw 15 (not default 100) to balance style transfer with prompt responsiveness
Prompt-based image editing: Upload existing image and describe desired change (new pose, new scene elements, different outfit) to preserve original composition while modifying specified elements

Custom GPT prompt generator: Upload Kling user guide and Nano Banana Pro guide to ChatGPT, instruct GPT to convert plain-language scene descriptions into complete production-ready prompts in Five-Part Cinematic structure

Kling 3.0 multi-shot generator: Upload official Kling user guide to custom GPT, instruct it to generate multi-shot sequences with per-shot timing estimates derived from script readthrough (keep heaviest dialogue near beginning to avoid sync drift in final seconds)

Shot-specific camera vocabulary: Handheld (naturalistic shake, documentary), Dolly in/out (smooth linear push, tension building), Crane (vertical/diagonal epic reveals), Arc (curved path around subject, dialogue coverage), Lateral pass (sideways travel), Static camera (preserve anatomy, subtle motion), Slow steady push-in (cinematic zoom, emotional beats)

operating_rules: Law I - Quality Chain: Output quality is bounded by weakest link in pipeline. Low-resolution input image caps video quality regardless of generation settings. Always select highest available resolution at every stage: 4K image output, Professional mode generation, 4K video upscaling. Pre-animation upscaling is highest-leverage quality improvement.

Law II - Prompt Precision: Prompt detail translates directly to output quality. Vague prompts produce generic results; specific prompts produce cinematic results. Specify camera type/lens, lighting direction, skin texture, clothing brands/materials, environmental details, atmospheric effects, film characteristics. Use structured frameworks as completeness checklists. Use negative prompts as quality floor.

Law III - Consistency: Use same reference image for every generation featuring same character. Any variation introduces drift. Maintain identical lighting conventions and camera grammar across prompts for visual continuity. Write one Style Bible Line and copy it across every prompt (only action line changes per shot). Kling preserves artistic integrity (color tone, contrast, lighting structure) from first frame better than competitors; make that foundation.

Law IV - Iteration: AI video generation is inherently stochastic. Same prompt with different seeds produces different results. Budget for 2-3 generations per shot and select best output. Treat prompting as directional, not deterministic. Favor subtle motions over dramatic ones in early iterations; push complexity gradually once stable base exists.

Law V - Control Hierarchy: Every production choice sits on control spectrum. Always use highest level of control production allows. Maximum control (Start + End frame, Elements, negative prompts) for critical shots/final deliverables/client-facing work. High control (Start frame only, Elements, negative prompts) for standard production shots/recurring characters. Medium control (Start frame only, no Elements) for exploratory shots/one-off scenes. Low control (Text-to-video) for rapid ideation/concept exploration only.

Law VI - Reference Role: Do not dump multiple reference images without direction. Each reference image must be assigned explicit role: one for lighting/color grading, another for environment design, a third for character identity with instructions to ignore irrelevant elements. Tag references explicitly (@image1, @image2, @image3) so model knows which visual information to extract from each source.

Law VII - Asset-First: High-quality AI filmmaking is no longer about raw generation; it is about governing consistency across fragmented AI tools. Production shifts from single prompt to asset library. Build Elements, Style Bibles, and motion references once, then compose into content infinitely. Operators internalizing this law produce at 10x velocity of those still prompting from scratch. Quality engineered at start of pipeline; post-production cannot save what pre-production did not build.

Dual-upscaling method: Run native upscaler in image generator first, then pass output through dedicated AI upscaler (Magnific) for intricate detail enhancement (wrinkles, hair strands, material textures, reflections). Alternatively, download generated image, re-upload as reference, and prompt for additional detail/sharpness preserving exact composition (hybrid upscale-edit technique).

Image-to-video is primary method, not text-to-video: Image-to-video gives less control than text-to-video, but with controlled start frame locks composition, character, and lighting from first frame, which is production default. Use text-to-video for exploration only.

Start frame only vs. Start and End frames: Start frame only when you want AI to determine ending, best for open-ended scenes with loose motion. Start and end frames when specific endpoint needed, generate both frames as images, describe transition for maximum control over shot arc. Note: Kling 1.0 sometimes outperforms later versions for start/end workflows.

Motion control vocabulary priority: Favor subtle motion (slowly, gently, subtle motion, static camera) over dramatic motion to preserve character anatomy. Large movements cause shape deformation. When dramatic motion needed, acquire via motion transfer instead: upload reference clip with desired camera movement and Kling will transfer motion path to new AI-generated scene.
Professional mode is mandatory: Professional mode preserves source image detail and produces more realistic lighting/motion. Standard mode visibly lower quality. Always enable.
Duration default 5 seconds maximum: Longer clips introduce deformation. Generate multiple 5-second clips and cut between them rather than pushing 10-15 seconds.
Creativity vs. Relevance toggle toward Relevance: Produces predictable prompt-adherent results. Move toward Creativity only for exploration.
Native audio enabled (Kling 2.6+): Integrated audio matches visual action, adds production value without post-processing.
Aspect ratio 16:9 standard: Use 9:16 or 1:1 only for platform-specific deliverables.
Always supply negative prompt: Acts as quality floor, prevents common failure modes before they occur.

Pre-flight checklist must precede every generation: Is reference at maximum resolution + upscaled? Is generation governed by Element if character/product involved? Is Style Bible Line present? Does prompt follow correct framework structure? Are preservation constraints explicit? Is negative prompt present and complete? Is model correct for shot type? Professional mode enabled? Native audio on? Aspect ratio correct? Resolution maximum? Duration 5 seconds or justified otherwise? Budget for 2-3 iterations? Run before generating to prevent wasted credits.

Element building minimum standard: 4+ reference images at different angles (close-up, full body, side profile, 3/4 view) minimum one with emotion variation. Upload bundle, auto-describe using chat tool, identity test in novel scene before deployment.

Product Element configuration: Upload separate images of product, background/staging, decorative elements as distinct Elements. Model composites into cohesive product video while maintaining logo integrity and detail fidelity. One product photoshoot plus AI environment generation replaces multiple location shoots, studio setups, seasonal reshoots.

Style Bible Line discipline: Write one sentence describing visual identity of entire project: camera system, film stock, color grade, aspect ratio, atmospheric tone. Copy across every prompt in project. Only action line changes per shot. Cheapest and most powerful consistency mechanism available, costs nothing to implement, removes entire categories of visual drift.

Character persistence across multiple tools (Kling + Midjourney + Runway + Flux): Curate four canonical angles (front, back, profile, face close-up) of character and feed same master reference sheet into every tool's context window. Re-prompt each tool to maintain specific traits. Professional AI studios eliminate uncanny valley across multi-tool pipeline through this method.

LoRA training economics: For series work or long-running channels with recurring character, train custom LoRA rather than rely on references alone. Feed 10-20 high-quality 1080p frontal-face video sequences into custom LoRA trainer (approximately 40 minutes training). Cost trivial relative to cost of re-shooting.

Kling version selection decision tree: Editing existing footage? -> Kling O1/Omni One or OmniEdit. 15-second multi-shot sequence with multiple angles or multi-character dialogue? -> Kling 3.0. Precise start frame + precise end frame both matter equally? -> Kling 1.0 first, Kling 2.6 fallback. Green-screen character for later compositing? -> Kling 2.5 Turbo. Standard 5-second narrative shot with Elements + native audio? -> Kling 2.6. Character-series pipeline with trained LoRA + reference-image anchoring? -> Kling 2.1 or 2.6 depending on feature needs.

Multi-shot generation best practices: Keep individual shot prompts under 500 characters or prompt adherence becomes unreliable. Move extra specificity into Element description or Style Bible Line. Keep heaviest spoken lines near beginning of 15-second sequence as dialogue drift and sync issues tend to appear in final seconds.

Green-screen pipeline: Generate or photograph character on green screen background -> Animate with Kling 2.5 Turbo (image-to-video) to create green-screen motion clip -> Use Kling O1/Omni One transformation: upload green-screen video plus reference image of desired environment, prompt to change background while keeping character/motion/proportions same -> Model composites character into new environment, adjusts shadows/reflections, relights to match new light source -> Optional: take composite into After Effects with shape layers and track mattes for split-screen or multi-environment VFX.

Lip-sync path options: (1) Type text and select AI voice (fastest, variable quality). (2) Generate voiceover in ElevenLabs first, upload audio file to Kling's lip-sync feature (professional standard, more natural results). Kling 3.0 multi-character lip-sync automatically identifies which character is speaking in each shot of multi-shot sequence and applies sync accordingly.

Image realism requirement for lip-sync: Realistic images produce better lip-sync than stylized images. Photorealistic faces and Renaissance-painting-style subjects sync well; heavily stylized artwork syncs poorly. Match image aesthetic to lip-sync needs.

OmniEdit operations (Kling O1): Element removal (describe what to remove, AI fills background, use for cleaning shots/removing logos/creating empty-city effects). Element addition (describe what to add like 'add gun in character hand'), AI composites into existing footage. Video restyle (change visual style via prompt while preserving camera motion, timing, character identity). Relighting (change lighting conditions, AI recalculates shadows/reflections/color temperature matching new light source to character geometry). Scene extension (upload short clip, generate next shot with consistent subject/environment, eliminates manual character-consistency workarounds). Multiple camera angles from one scene (upload video, prompt for new angle, AI regenerates scene from that perspective with environment/character intact).
AI transitions operation: Feed last frame of clip A and first frame of clip B into start/end-frame generation with transition description, place result between clips for seamless creative transition.

Shot switching from existing clips: Upload clip and prompt for different camera angle (close-up, wide shot, low angle, top-down, aerial). Kling regenerates scene from new angle while maintaining subject consistency. Build coverage without regenerating from scratch.

Monetization positioning archetypes: (1) The AI Cinema Director: film-quality output at 1/10th cost of traditional live-action, premium price point, agency and indie-film buyers. (2) The AI VFX Studio: cinematic VFX from your pocket with no After Effects expertise required, mid-to-premium price, creator and creator-economy buyers. (3) The Brand Content Engine: unlimited on-brand video production at subscription cost, recurring retainer, SMB and D2C brands. (4) The Cinematic AI Operator: finished short-form narratives not raw AI footage, per-project pricing, creator-agencies and platforms.

Mindset shift 1 - Gambling to Engineering: AI video not a slot machine. Structured prompts, reference images, and Elements make output predictable. Budget for iteration but reduce randomness systematically. Work is more like software engineering than traditional filmmaking; debug generations, not wait for inspiration.

Mindset shift 2 - Post-Production to Pre-Production: Quality ceiling set before you hit generate. Image quality, upscaling, Element preparation, prompt structure matter more than post-processing. Most operators over-invest in post, under-invest in pre; invert that ratio and output quality rises sharply.

Mindset shift 3 - Single-Shot to Pipeline Thinking: Value is in complete chain (image -> upscale -> animate -> upscale -> edit), not any individual generation. Optimize pipeline as whole, not steps in isolation. Slightly worse animation on 4K reference beats slightly better animation on 1K reference every time.

Mindset shift 4 - Manual VFX to AI Compositing: Operations that required After Effects, Nuke, or 3D tools (relighting, environment compositing, element removal) can now be done with prompt. Barrier to VFX-quality output has collapsed. Operators who internalize this first will absorb entire mid-tier of traditional VFX market before market knows it is being absorbed.

contradictions: Kling 1.0 sometimes outperforms later versions (2.6, 3.0) for specific start/end frame workflows despite being older, contradicting typical expectation that newer versions always superior for all tasks
weird_gold: Angles 2.0 workflow: Upload base image and auto-generate 12 optimized camera angles without additional prompting, replacing manual storyboarding entirely with AI-generated coverage
Hybrid live-action pipeline: Green-screen shot on phone used as motion reference for Kling to transfer motion path to AI-generated scene, collapsing traditional live-action/CGI boundary
Custom LoRA training cost economics: 40-minute training time produces series consistency approaching traditional casting level, trivial cost relative to reshooting
AI Director Mode: Describe scene and model generates establishing shots, close-ups, cuts automatically, replacing manual shot planning for simple sequences
Reference role assignment tagging: Explicit @image1 @image2 @image3 naming prevents reference confusion and forces model to extract only designated visual information from each source
Lighting transfer technique: Separate reference images for lighting/color and composition, merged in single generation to combine color palette of one image with framing of another
Midjourney style-weight discovery: Default --sw 100 overrides prompt control; --sw 15 balances style transfer with prompt responsiveness, requiring deliberate undersetting
Asset-First paradigm shift: Once Elements/Style Bibles/motion references built once, infinite content composition follows, producing 10x velocity vs. prompt-from-scratch operators
Five-minute generation limit: Optimal output at 5 seconds; longer clips deform, requiring multiple 5-second clips cut together instead of pushing single longer clip
Multi-character lip-sync intelligence: Kling 3.0 automatically identifies which character is speaking in each multi-shot sequence and applies sync accordingly without manual per-character direction
OmniEdit surgical editing: Constraint Sandwich structure (Anchor + Action + Preserve) prevents model license to drift, explicit preservation constraints most commonly omitted but most important block

Image-to-video primacy: Reversed intuition that text-to-video is primary (it gives LESS control); image-to-video with controlled start frame standard because it locks composition, character, lighting from frame 1
